title: API Behavioral Probe Matrix and Prospectivity Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a repeatable, region-aware API Behavioral Probe Matrix and an associated playbook that product managers and solutions engineers can use to evaluate competitor inference endpoints and open-model variants. The deliverable will codify probe types, synthetic workloads, measurement heuristics, and a prospectivity scoring method to translate observed behavioral differences into sales and product actions (fallback decisions, packaging opportunities, ROI narratives).
objectives: Define a taxonomy of API behaviors relevant to Redwood customers (rate-limit shapes, tail error modes, deterministic vs nondeterministic outputs, tokenization deltas, streaming semantics, function-calling fidelity, structured output stability, safety filter false-positive rates).

Assemble a reproducible probe harness that can run across multi-region endpoints and private deployment variants and produce comparable metrics (latency P50/P90/P99, error class distribution, token-cost variance, hallucination proxies, content-filtering incidence).

Produce a prospectivity scoring model that converts probe results into go/no-go signals for commercial plays (e.g., price-sensitive fallback candidate, high-uptime partner for SLA guarantees, disqualify for regulated verticals).
Ship a Playbook (one-pager + actionable runbook) for GTM, sales engineering, and SRE to operationalize competitor signals into procurement guidance and customer conversations.
success_metrics: Probe harness able to run 3 canonical workloads across 4 regions in < 24 hours
Prospectivity score correlates with customer-reported latency or SLA complaints in 7/10 pilot accounts
Playbook adopted by solutions engineering for at least two RFPs within 6 weeks of delivery
Dataset of competitor API behaviors with changelog maintained weekly
tasks: Kickoff meeting with SE and SRE to align on safe probing constraints and rate limits
Inventory competitor endpoints and open-model variants to include in first run (3 proprietary, 4 open-source builds)
Define 5 synthetic workload templates: chat-short, chat-long, instruction-batch, embedding-bulk, structured-output-verify
Implement harness: retries, region rotation, token accounting, deterministic seeds where applicable
Run baseline sweep across us-west, us-east, eu-west and ap-southeast regions and collect metrics
Analyze and normalize results, produce API Behavioral Matrix CSV and an initial prospectivity ranking
Draft Playbook: scoring rubric, recommended fallback categories, sales talking points, limitations
Review with Legal for acceptable external probing and with Security for data handling and sandboxing
Publish results to Confluence, attach dashboards, and brief GTM + Solutions Engineering
acceptance_criteria: Probe harness executes end-to-end without causing rate-limit penalties in >80% of runs (or includes documented backoff handling)
Matrix includes P50/P90/P99, classified error buckets, token-cost delta vs Redwood baseline, and structured-output fidelity score
Playbook contains at least three example prospectivity-to-action mappings (e.g., when to recommend Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API)
Stakeholders (SE, Sales, SRE) sign off on playbook and dataset format
risks: Probing may trigger vendor rate-limits or temporary blocks; must have SRE/Legal guardrails
Open-model variants may be updated mid-sweep causing noncomparable results; need changelogging
Interpretation risk: measured differences may not map cleanly to customer experience without qualitative follow-up
Storage of competitor outputs could create legal/terms-of-service implications—avoid storing PII and redact outputs
decisions_needed: Scope of competitor set for first wave (max 7 endpoints)
Whether to include community mirrors of closed APIs (legal review required)
Standardized seed/temperature policy for deterministic comparison
Tolerance thresholds for classifying a model as 'enterprise-ready' vs 'fallback candidate'
timeline: Week 0: kickoff and scope; Week 1: harness implementation; Week 2: baseline runs; Week 3: analysis and scoring; Week 4: playbook and stakeholder review; Week 5: publish and GTM handoff
